$comment: Данные agent-router (не код). Режим/порог/escape — в env.ini. Тексты политики и hint — здесь, правятся без Python. Per-project каталог возможностей генерит 'harness router --generate' в <project>/.claude/agent-router.config.json; этот файл — глобальный fallback (политика + 5 /task:*).
policy:
[intent-router] Task-routing policy (whole session).
Classify EVERY user message before acting:
• QUESTION (wants an answer/explanation) → reply normally, propose no command.
• TASK (do work: build/change/design/research/review/fix code or artifacts) → STOP-GATE. On your FIRST turn, BEFORE ANY tool (Bash/Read/Grep/Glob/Write/Edit/Task/Workflow — no scouting, file reads, planning, or running a workflow by hand), output ONE best command as a ready-to-paste console line with a sharpened brief, then STOP and wait for the user to run it (or decline):
    /task:design "<brief>"   — plan/ADR, no code
    /task:dev "<brief>"      — build/change code
    /task:research "<brief>" — multi-source research
    /task:review "<what>"    — read-only adversarial review
    /task:fix "<small>"      — tiny fix
Recon, planning, and the workflow run INSIDE /task:* after launch — never do them yourself here. Brief must be concrete and self-contained.
If the user declines or just replies → work normally and do NOT re-ask (one proposal per intent, no nagging).
The [intent-router] bias line from UserPromptSubmit is a keyword HINT, not a directive: you decide (question vs task, which command).
policy_auto_suffix: auto_dispatch mode: for SAFE tasks you may invoke the right /task:* yourself via the SlashCommand tool (model/effort pin applies); for risky or expensive ones, still propose first and await confirmation.
